# fastf 3.2.0 — what a preview promises is what a create writes

fastf is developed on Linux, and its Windows build is compiled by CI but never
driven. This release is what happened when it was: a live suite on a real NTFS
volume and a real SMB share, two Windows defects it found on its first run, and
eight more it reproduced along the way — none of which turned out to be about
Windows at all.

## A dry run listed one thing and previewed another

The "Files:" section of `fastf new --dry-run` walked the real template and
applied its `exclude` globs. The "Previews:" section below it did not: it read
the in-memory buffer of every text file in the template, so a file you had
excluded was previewed with a body it would never have, and a `verbatim` file —
one whose `{braces}` are meant to reach the project literally — was previewed
with them filled in. Two answers to one question, on one screen.

There is one answer now. A single classifier decides what happens to each file,
and the preview, the copy and `fastf apply`'s plan all ask it, so they cannot
drift apart. An excluded file appears nowhere; a verbatim one is previewed
exactly as it will be written, and says so. `fastf apply` also stopped asking
for variables that nothing it writes could use.

## A template is the folder it lives in

Copy a template folder, edit half of it, and forget the `slug:` line inside
`template.yaml`, and fastf listed it under the name in the manifest — a name
that every other command then rejected, pointing you back at the list that had
just printed it. Worse, two folders could claim the same slug, and creating from
the second one silently created the first: right ID, wrong files, no error.

The folder's name is the slug. A manifest that disagrees still works, under the
name every command accepts, and `fastf template show` tells you the two differ.
Saving that template through fastf repairs it.

## Questions fastf could not read, answered anyway

`fastf search created<tomorrow` matched every project you have, because
`created` holds a date and the comparison is on the text. `fastf recent --since
2026-6-1` silently hid the whole year, for want of two zeroes. `created>`,
`tag:`, a `--base` that names nothing and a `--template` that names nothing all
printed "no projects match" and exited successfully.

All of them are refused now, by name, with the real answers listed — the guided
app's search bar has done this as you type since it was written, and the command
line simply never asked it. And `key=*value*`, which the documentation has
always called a glob, matches what it looks like it matches: a `*` may lead,
trail, or do both.

## Windows, from a real Windows machine

**A read-only file blocked every metadata write.** fastf publishes a metadata
update by renaming over the old file, and Windows refuses that when the target
is marked read-only — which is how a project arrives from a backup, from
read-only media, or from a cloud client. Tagging, renaming, noting, moving and
the ID counter all failed with `Access is denied`. The attribute is set aside
for the rename and put back on the published file: your marking is kept, and the
update lands.

**A case-only rename of a non-ASCII name was refused as its own target.** NTFS
is case-insensitive over Cyrillic and Greek too; fastf's check was not, so
renaming `проект` to `ПРОЕКТ` failed, naming the very folder you were renaming.
The identical rename in English always worked, which is why no test had ever
seen it.

## Also

`fastf id show` prints the counter as the number it is, rather than through the
first template that happened to sort first — it could show the same value twice
in two spellings on one line. `fastf template show` no longer promises to copy
files that fastf drops. `fastf template from-folder` stopped writing Windows'
`\\?\` path prefix into a template's description, and the refusal for a project
whose metadata has vanished says what actually went missing.

## Upgrading

Install 3.2.0. Nothing to migrate: templates, projects and caches are unchanged,
and a template whose manifest disagrees with its folder is repaired the next time
you save it.
